method_notes: I picked 30 SRS guests from May 2025 to Oct 2026 who weren't household names (20 non-military, 10 military/LE/intel) using episode listings on Shortform, Singju Post, Apple and Spotify. For each guest I searched for podcast appearances and kept the date and source URL. Only appearances confirmed in the 12 months before the SRS episode count toward the tally (in_12mo_window=true). Appearances that came after SRS were left out. Older or undated ones are kept with in_12mo_window=false/null as context. LIMITS: the session's web-search cap ran out at about 90 searches into this task, so most guests got only 1-2 searches. Earlier appearances are badly under-sampled, and every tally count is a floor, not a full count. Audience sizes, Spotify show URLs and booking routes did not come up in searches, so they are marked unverified or null; no URLs or emails were guessed. Episode dates come from search snippets: exact for most episodes, approximated from neighboring episode numbers for #284, #293, #316 and #336. Hosts who later became SRS guests: Tucker Carlson (#256), Joe Lonsdale (#302), Dave Ramsey (Ramsey Network; date not confirmed). Shawn Ryan also went on The Diary of a CEO in 2026. Networks and agencies that came up: Tucker Carlson Network (Steve Robinson's documentary partnership), Ramsey Network (2 shows for one guest), Colossus (Invest Like the Best), and speaker bureaus (Worldwide Speakers Group for Vescovo, Champions Speakers for Montgomery). No podcast-specific booking agency came up.

patterns: Non-military guests mostly reach SRS on the back of a fresh, newsworthy moment: a viral investigation (Shirley, Robinson, Schlep), a funding or tech milestone (Scholl, Adcock, Bry, Taylor), or a book or discovery. That moment gets picked up first by a large business or culture show (Tucker, PBD, JRE, DOAC, Moonshots), usually 1-10 months before SRS. Defense-relevant tech founders tend to arrive through a cluster of VC and founder shows (Logan Bartlett, StrictlyVC, Relentless, American Optimist, Moonshots), while faith and mystery guests come through Blurry Creatures and Tucker. SRS also books from its own network: repeat guests (Luna, Montgomery, Shirley), guests linked to earlier guests (Schlep and Montgomery on Roblox), and hosts of feeder shows (Tucker, Lonsdale, Ramsey).
avery_path: Start with story-driven business shows where Avery fits naturally: The Jordan Harbinger Show, PBD Podcast and The Diary of a CEO, pitching the Alec Monopoly brand-building story and ArtLife's early move online. Add one tech or abundance show (Moonshots or American Optimist) for the early-tech-adoption angle, and one investigative or crime show (Julian Dorey, or Tucker if there's a real exposé) for an art-crime or provenance angle. Tie the run to a concrete news hook, such as a major sale, an ArtLife milestone, a celebrity collaboration or a conservation auction, because SRS books non-military guests around a fresh moment. Then pitch SRS directly on angles that match its audience: his work with the Miami Police 'Do the Right Thing' program, art-market crime and money laundering, and conservation philanthropy, with the earlier episodes as social proof. Look for a warm introduction through an SRS alumnus (e.g., a Miami or Florida-based guest such as Ryan Montgomery, whose company is in Boca Raton).
